correctness.rationale: For \(n=2^r\ge4\) and \(q=2^f\), use \(R=\mathbb F_q[z,z^{-1}]/((z+1)^n)\) and \(c=(z+1)^2/z\). The graph adjacency is \(A=\begin{psmallmatrix}c&1\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix}\), invertible with \((A+I)^2=cA\). The temporal operator satisfies \(T^2+\mathcal AT+I=0\) and \(T^3+I=(T+I)(\mathcal A+I)T\), with both exterior factors invertible. The fixed space at time \(3\cdot2^j\) has dimension \(4\cdot2^j\) for \(0\le j\le r\). Every nonzero primitive period is divisible by three, hence consecutive fixed-population differences give the complete counts and sharp order \(3n\). Actual standalone programs exhaustively checked all 65,536 binary states for \(n=4\) and computed exact binary operator ranks for \(n=4,8,16,32,64\). These tests are not a proof for all sizes or fields.

value.rationale: Power-of-two circumferences are a natural characteristic-two degeneration regime. Attaching a single leaf per cycle site changes the exact temporal order from \(n\) to \(3n\) and introduces primitive periods \(3\cdot2^j\), with an explicit state and orbit census over every \(\mathbb F_{2^f}\). This graph-perturbation phenomenon is mathematically motivated, rather than an arbitrary finite census. The proof resolves the entire natural dyadic family without claiming a general corona result.
